name: London Metropolitan University

sources.title: Compliance Interview Guide - London Metropolitan University
topics: Intention to Study in the UK
quotes: Why do you want to study in the UK?
Benefits of studying in the UK compared to your home country or other countries
What motivated your choice of course at London Met?
Which modules are you most interested in and why?
Why do you prefer your London Met course compared to similar courses at other universities?
How does your course fit into your long-term career plans?
What roles or types of organisations do graduates from your course typically enter?
Do you understand your responsibilities as a UK Student Visa holder?
Who is financing your tuition fees and living costs?
sources.notes: Fetched. This is London Met's own compliance (pre-CAS) interview guide; page says interviews are 'a standard part of the process' for applicants from specific countries after meeting offer conditions. No platform, length or outcome details on the page.

sources.title: Credibility interviews - London Metropolitan University
topics: immigration history: previous UK visas held, whether visa conditions were ever breached, visas obtained for other countries
study plans: gap between previous study and new course, reasons for choosing London Met and your course, plans after the course
financial matters: where your money has come from, family circumstances and financial support
quotes: If there is a long gap between previous study and your new course you may be asked to explain why there has been a break
You may be asked about your plans after the course, eg where do you want to work
UKVI may ask where your money has come from
sources.notes: Fetched. Describes the UKVI (Home Office) credibility interview 'via a video link with a member of staff from the Home Office'. Advice: 'be able to talk about the course content and not just list the modules'.

sources.title: Visa Information | London Metropolitan University Study Centre
sources.notes: Fetched. Pathway centre page: 'You must complete a Pre-CAS interview to allow us to assess whether your chosen course meets the vis requirements and whether you fulfil the criteria to study in the UK.' Minimum £4,000 deposit before CAS request. No questions.
